newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut down in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut down in profit-taking.

text.p: Two of three listed bank shares were steady on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday while newcomer Bank of Beirut fell 1.7 percent in profit-taking.
Dealers said strong demand for Bank of Beirut and the bank's strong fundamentals would sustain the share's current price level.
"It is a temporary period of profit-taking," Alain Balian, Deputy Manager at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest told Reuters.
"It is temporary because many people have bought at $3.5 or above and they will not be willing to sell now," he added.
Bank of Beirut traded at $3.5625 from Tuesday's $3.625. Demand was 399,390 against a supply of 578,129 shares. Turnover was 310,501 shares compared with 629,606 a day earlier.
The share, which made its debut on April 11, has risen 64 percent over it share price issue.
Some 10,000 and 25,000 Bank of Beirut shares changed hands in two separate blocks on the floor at $3.75 and $3.6875 respectively.
"The block trades also indicate investor interest in the share. Investors buying at $3.5 are shooting at the $4 and above," Balian added.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi held steady at $15.625 and $20 respectively. Both banks traded in heavy demand.
A block trade of 23,000 Audi shares traded off the floor at $20 while a block of 2,500 BLC shares traded on the floor at $15.625.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.58 percent to 134.94. The BLOM general index rose 0.001 percent to 911.52 and the LISPI rose 0.13 percent to 87.06.
Pipemaker Eternit rose to $20 from $1.9375 on turnover of 26,500 shares from 44,500 a day earlier.
Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.25 on turnover of 500 shares againt Tuesday's 500.
Total BSE turnover fell to 514,749 shares, almost half Tuesday's 915,701 and value was $3,075,143 from $5,610,320.
Solidere A and B shares were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75 respectively.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
